// Expected values for the baker's work (docs/rules/baking.md), captured from the original program in the emulator (ADR 0008):
// tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb goods with a finished bakery (type 16, a large building) at a flag, reduced to the passes that
// matter. The building's flag pointer (+0xe, which its handler 0x42e37e keeps its flour request through) is set by hand, as a built site
// leaves it (0x43ef82). A scenario starts with a "#" line that names its verb command; each line after it gives, for a pass, the 16 bytes
// of the baker (slot 3, s3=: a settler without a job that the castle makes the baker) where his node, state, or part of the work changed,
// the 18 bytes of the building (b=, its flag pointer left out) where they changed, the flag's byte 4 and goods bytes (g=) where they
// changed, the request words of the flag (req=, the bytes 0x42 to 0x45) where they changed, the castle's flour count (flour=) and bread
// count (bread=) where they changed, and the generator's words (rng=) as they stand. The puts of the command lay the flour on the
// places of the castle's flag (slot 1) or of another flag by hand. The flags are listed in the order the engine numbers them (by column).
// The scenario store-full lays seven flours on the far flag (slot 3) at the pass 600 and an eighth on the castle's flag (slot 2) at 700:
// the bakery takes eight (its rank 0xff shifted right by the flours it holds is 1 at seven, and the serve of the eighth halves it to 0),
// and the ninth goes to the castle (flour=1). Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.
